Through :- Mr. Suneel Malhotra, Advocate with  Mr. Divyanshu Malhotra, Advocate for R-1.
Coram: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE PUNEET GUPTA, JUDGE  JUDGMENT 1.
Respondent Nos. 2 & 3 are set ex-parte in the appeal.

2. The claim petition was filed by the appellants herein before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Jammu whereby the appellants sought compensation on account of death of Bhuvan Sachdev.
3. The claim petition was contested by the respondents herein.

The claim petition was dismissed primarily on the basis of findings recorded on Issue no.1 which pertains to the factum of proving rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the petitioners therein.
4. The learned counsel appearing for the appellants has argued that the Tribunal has erred in recording that the Issue no.1 is not proved by the appellants herein.
The evidence on record produced by the petitioners does make out that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the truck which was also involved in the accident.
The reliance placed upon the FIR and the investigations carried out in the matter by the police agency could not be the sole criteria for depriving the appellants of their genuine claim.

5. The learned counsel appearing for the respondent-Company has submitted that the petitioners in Vijay Pati Sachdev And Others vs National Insurance Company Lt. And on 16 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187137119/

sentences.text: the claim petition failed to prove the issue before the Tribunal and the finding of the Tribunal is not wrong in the facts and circumstances of the case which may require any interference by this Court.
6. The scanned record of the Tribunal is before the Court.

7. It was pleaded in the claim petition filed before the Tribunal that on 29.10.2006 at about 10.20 PM the said Bhuvan Sachdev along with his friend Narinder Singh was on way from Satwari to Apna Vihar on a motor cycle and when the vehicle reached at Digiana, the offending vehicle (Truck) came from behind at a very high speed, overtook the motor cycle and suddenly stopped in the middle of the road on non- parking place without any signal as a result the motor cycle of the deceased hit the truck on back side as a result the said Bhuvan Sachdev and Narinder Singh received injuries.

Bhuvan Sachdev was immediately shifted to Government Medical College, Jammu and thereafter to Acharya Shri Chander College of Medical Science and Hospital, Jammu where he remained admitted from 30.10.2006 to 10.11.2006.

entities.text: Acharya Shri Chander College of Medical Science and Hospital, Jammu
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The said Bhuvan Sachdev died on 10.11.2006.
The respondent-driver in his reply to the claim petition denied that the accident was caused due to negligent act of the said respondent.
8. The respondent-Insurance Company denied the accident for want of knowledge though it was not denied that the vehicle was insured with the Insurance Company.
9. The petitioners produced Rohit Singh as a witness, who is stated to have witnessed the occurrence.
The other evidence produced by the petitioners pertains to the income of the deceased at the time of accident.
It may be mentioned herein that Vijay Pati, father of the deceased, had also appeared as a witness though he was not witness to the accident.
The respondent-driver has appeared as his own witness in the case.
Mohd. Rafiq has also appeared as a witness qua the investigations which have been carried out in the matter.

10. PW-Rohit Singh in his statement has mentioned that on 29.10.2006 he was on his way to home from factory and when reached near Digiana Bridge, a truck bearing JK02D/1670 overtook the motor cycle as a result the motorcyclist hit the truck from behind and fell down.
The truck was being driven at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner by its driver.
Both the persons on the motorcycle received injuries and shifted to GMC, Jammu.
On cross-examination, the witness negated the suggestion that the motorcyclist was on a high speed.
It is also wrong to state that truck and motorcycle were overtaking each other.
He also went to GMC and then to Batra Hospital.
The driver-Mohan Lal in his statement has altogether denied that his truck hit the motorcyclist and caused the accident though he also admits that he was driving the truck at that time.

11. RW-Mohd. Rafiq has not investigated the FIR No. 287/2006 registered with Police Station,
Gandhi Nagar, Jammu for the offences under Sections 279/337 RPC though he has produced the investigation carried out in the case by Incharge Police Post, Diginana, namely, Varinder Gupta.
As per him, the investigation was closed as untraceable.
The Sub-Inspector, Ajay Sharma, had concluded that it was Motor Cycle No. 1251/JKU which caused the accident with the truck which was parked on the road side.
RW-Mohd. Rafiq has only relied upon the investigation of the I.O and nothing more.
He has not investigated the matter.

The Tribunal has heavily relied upon the statement of Mohd. Rafiq Khan in order to hold that the petitioners were not able to prove the issue of rash and negligent driving by the driver of the truck,
Mohan Lal.

The statement of PW-Rohit Singh has been held to be fabrication of the case but without stating how the Tribunal reached such conclusion.
13.

The statement of Mohd. Rafiq Khan should not have led the Tribunal to nullify the case of the petitioners for the simple reason that he had not conducted the investigation and he only mentions of the closure of the case on the basis of investigation which had been carried out by other police officer.
14. The statement of Rohit Singh could not be shattered during cross- examination.

The witness has mentioned that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the truck bearing No. JK02D/1670 as the driver of truck overtook the motor cycle which resulted into hitting of the motor cycle with the truck.
It may be mentioned herein that the registration number of the motor cycle was 1251/JKU.
The statement of the driver of the truck is itself vague and simply states of his truck being not involved in the accident.

There was no reason for the Tribunal not to rely upon the statement of PW-Rohit Singh and brush aside the negligence of the driver of the trunk only on the basis of the some investigation carried out in the FIR which did not hold the truck driver liable for accident.
15. It is trite proposition of law that in a case filed under the Motor Vehicle Act, standard of proof of the rash and negligent act is not to be assessed as is required in a criminal trial.
The probabilities are required to be seen while deciding the issue of rash and negligent act in a petition filed under the Motor Vehicles Act.
16. In 2023 Live Law (SC) 531, the Hon'ble Apex Court while dealing with a case under the Motor Vehicles Act held that preponderance of possibilities is required to be seen.
The case cannot be thrown out on the basis of investigation carried in criminal case.

17. In (2018) 12 SCC 15, the Hon'ble Apex Court did not agree with the findings of the High Court which were based purely on the ground that the FIR which was lodged on the complaint of the appellant contained a version which was at variance with the evidence which emerged before the Tribunal.

18. The learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company has relied upon 1977 Legal Eagle (SC) 65 and 2007 ACJ 1928 in support of his contention that the petitioner had failed to prove the rash and negligent driving on part of the so called offending vehicle (truck).
In this authority, the court had taken note of the fact that both the parties had relied upon FIR though the contents of the documents had not been proved.
In the case in hand, the petitioners had only brought on record copy of FIR and nothing more.

The investigation in the FIR in the present case should not have come in the way of the Tribunal to assess independently the evidence brought on record by the claimants Vijay Pati Sachdev And Others vs National Insurance Company Lt.

3 19.
The Court, in the facts and circumstances of the case, is of the view that the Tribunal has not decided the Issue No.1 correctly.
The petitioners have been able to prove through their evidence that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the truck, respondent No.3 in the appeal.
The findings of the Tribunal on Issue No.1 are set aside and the issue is decided in favour of the appellants herein.
20. The claim petition of the appellants stood dismissed on finding given by the Tribunal on Issue No.1 only.
The Court is of the view that for deciding the other issues the matter is required to be remanded back to the Tribunal.
The Tribunal shall decide the matter on priority keeping in view the evidence that has come on record before it.
21. Learned counsels for the parties are directed to appear before the Tribunal on 28.09.2023.
